label: moss
color_rule: Black ink with #4f7031 green accents; fixed light-surface variant matching the landing header
quote: One ink splash; reads as a palmately lobed leaf. The colour is distance, not identity.

label: GitHub
color_rule: Black only (Invertocat), white optional on dark backgrounds; unmodified, secondary to moss's own mark
quote: Use a permitted GitHub logo to inform others that your project integrates with GitHub.

label: Cloudflare
color_rule: Official Cloudflare press-kit logo, displayed unmodified by explicit product decision
quote: Use of the Cloudflare logos (other than the use of Web Badges described below) requires our written permission.

label: IPFS
color_rule: Blue primary (#0B7EEB); Simple Icons monochrome trace

label: Tor Project
color_rule: Official Tor Project logo from its brand-assets page, displayed unmodified by explicit product decision
quote: If you have written permission to use a logo / graphic Tor Mark, like our "Tor Onion" logo, you must use it in the form in which it is made available at https://styleguide.torproject.org/brand-assets. You may not alter the color, font, proportions, or any other aspect of our logo.

label: Email
color_rule: Generic glyph; adapts to currentColor

label: Matters
color_rule: Two overlapping gradient circles (teal #D7EAE1→#79B1A6 over gold #F4E2BC→#BF9F5E) — Matters' actual favicon mark, used unmodified
quote: No formal brand or press guidelines page exists for Matters; this is the site's own official icon, taken verbatim from its source repo

label: Caddy
color_rule: Official Caddy site logo, displayed unmodified by explicit product decision
quote: The name "Caddy" is trademarked. The name of the software is "Caddy", not "Caddy Server" or "CaddyServer". Please call it "Caddy" or, if you wish to clarify, "the Caddy web server". Caddy is a registered trademark of Stack Holdings GmbH.

label: NGINX
color_rule: Official nginx.org logo, displayed unmodified by explicit product decision
quote: No right, license or permission is granted to use F5's trademarks except as may be provided explicitly by F5, Inc.

label: Amazon S3
color_rule: Official Amazon Simple Storage Service architecture icon from the current AWS icon package, displayed unmodified by explicit product decision
quote: Any use of the AWS Marks or Program Content outside the scope of the foregoing licenses requires Licensor's prior written permission.

label: Netlify
color_rule: Dark teal badge (#014847) with cyan mark (#32E6E2) — Netlify's own "encapsulated" format
quote: The encapsulated logo version works well when the background graphics are too busy to see the monogram version clearly or when Netlify is presented alongside other logos in an encapsulated format, such as a logo garden or directory site.

label: Vercel
color_rule: Black primary (currentColor); white on dark backgrounds
quote: The Vercel symbol should only be used in places where there is not enough room to display the full logo, or in cases where only brand symbols of multiple brands are displayed.

label: Codeberg
color_rule: Blue (#2185D0) and green are Codeberg's primary brand colors
quote: Logo material is licensed under CC0.

label: Self-hosted
color_rule: Generic glyph; adapts to currentColor

label: Nostr
color_rule: Purple (#662482) glyph on transparent, unmodified. A community-designed mark (Andrea Nicolini / Bembureda), not a company trademark — Nostr is protocol-only with no brand authority to grant or withhold permission
quote: In order to ensure the widest reach, Andrea released his work for the Nostr community under the Creative Commons Zero v1.0 Universal (CC0) license.

label: Secure Scuttlebutt
color_rule: Official scuttlebutt.nz Hermies mascot, displayed unmodified by explicit product decision

label: Willow
color_rule: Official willowprotocol.org favicon, displayed unmodified by explicit product decision

label: AT Protocol
color_rule: Official atproto.com favicon, displayed unmodified by explicit product decision

label: ActivityPub
color_rule: Pink/grey gradient icon-only symbol (the square mark from the same lockup as the wordmark logo), unmodified. The file's own embedded RDF metadata independently declares the same CC0 grant
quote: ActivityPub logo by mray, released into public domain under CC0 1.0.

label: Hypercore
color_rule: N/A — no file held. Route 1: holepunchto/hypercore carries a code LICENSE but no logo file in the repo; searched the whole holepunchto org for a brand/logo/press/design repo and found none. Route 2: pears.com's footer has only privacy/terms links, no license statement. Route 3: Holepunch is a real, Tether/Bitfinex-backed company, so unlike SSB/Willow this isn't obviously unregistered — but no specific trademark registration was confirmed this session, and there's simply no asset to attach one to yet

label: Iroh
color_rule: Official Iroh project wordmark, displayed unmodified by explicit product decision
quote: Copyright 2025 N0, INC. This project is licensed under either of Apache License, Version 2.0 ... or MIT license ... at your option.

label: Radicle
color_rule: Official radicle.dev pixel mark, displayed unmodified by explicit product decision

label: Gemini
color_rule: N/A — no file held. Route 1/2: re-fetched geminiprotocol.net raw; the page has zero tags, no favicon reference, and no GitHub/GitLab link anywhere — there is truly nothing to license, not just nothing I could find a policy for. Route 3: an informal, deliberately non-commercial project (Solderpunk and contributors; site content itself is CC BY-NC-ND) with no registered trademark. A real fit for moss regardless — a gemtext capsule is just another page format. Not to be confused with Google's Gemini AI or the Gemini crypto exchange, both of which likely do hold registered marks in unrelated classes

label: Filecoin
color_rule: Official filecoin.io icon, displayed unmodified by explicit product decision

label: Arweave
color_rule: Official black glyph, extracted unchanged from the Arweave website repository’s GlyphSVG.zip; CC BY-ND.
quote: Our brand materials are open-source and registered under Creative Commons (BY-ND). You are free to use and distribute the original files on your project. However, as we want to keep our identity consistent, derivatives are currently not allowed.
